correctness.rationale: For rank-one S=I−T, S²=λS. For λ≤1/5, the fourth power has norm at least 244/125; for λ>1/5, the projection P=I−S/λ is recovered from Cesàro means with norm strictly below c whenever ||T||≤1+r²/10^6, contradiction. Graph embedding transfers this lower bound from each base summand to any finite ℓ∞-sum. The component models and constants are explicit published theorems, the rational coefficient comparison is exact, and every n≥6 is 3a+4b. The finite checker validates only arithmetic, not external computer-aided inputs or the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Both seed papers provide dimension-specific projection bounds, while the complete relevant 2026 theorem proves only a non-numerical all-dimensional constant and explicitly flags non-effectivity. An elementary rank-one Cesàro argument derives an actual universal δ(c) and a specified rational all-dimensional gap. No equivalent effective stronger conclusion emerged from source statements or 13 targeted published-finding corpus searches. Residual risk: older 1976 source not inspected in full and indexing may miss effective versions.

value.rationale: The classical natural projection constant question asked for uniformity in dimension. The 2015 bound decreases with dimension, and a later uniform-existence theorem does not give an effective numerical value. An explicit operator-level modulus independent of dimension and number of blocks yields a concrete rational all-dimensional bound; quantitative effectivity is the substantive objective even though the coefficient is numerically very small.
